q: An 85-year-old man with mild dementia has developed cataracts, hearing loss, mild heart failure, and osteoarthritis during the past year. His family asks why several problems have appeared together. Which concept in Hazzard provides a biological framework for age-related changes across organ systems?
o: Aging is understood as disease that affects several organ systems.
Aging is understood as development directly shaped by natural selection.
Aging is understood as coordinated change across multiple organ systems.
Aging is understood as increased lifespan following a beneficial intervention.
explanation:
**Coordinated aging** refers to a shared physiological and molecular basis for changes in multiple tissues, rather than a diagnosis of the cause of each finding in this patient (application of the framework, p. 4). Experimental caloric restriction supports this framework because "nearly all of the consequences of aging are coordinately delayed" (p. 4).

**A. Aging is understood as disease that affects several organ systems.** Wrong, Hazzard explicitly distinguishes aging from disease: diseases are consequences of aging, but aging also produces changes not classified as disease (p. 4).
**B. Aging is understood as development directly shaped by natural selection.** Wrong, the text distinguishes development, which is directly shaped by natural selection, from aging, which reflects failure of selection to preserve function at seldom-reached ages (p. 4).
**C. Aging is understood as coordinated change across multiple organ systems.** Correct, the source describes a physiological and molecular basis that tends to synchronize multiple changes in older individuals; this is the framework asked about (p. 4).
**D. Aging is understood as increased lifespan following a beneficial intervention.** Wrong, life expectancy is influenced by factors besides aging, so an increase in lifespan does not by itself demonstrate an effect on aging (p. 4).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 4.
label: Source: Hazzard 8e (marked) · p.4

q: A 77-year-old man with diabetes, heart failure (ejection fraction 40%), and mild dementia attends a geriatric clinic. His wife reports two falls in the past month, missed medication despite pill organizers, and inability to manage household finances. She works full time and feels overwhelmed. He takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, furosemide 40 mg daily, carvedilol 12.5 mg twice daily, and donepezil 10 mg daily. HbA1c is 9.1%, creatinine 1.6, and eGFR 42. Which model explicitly uses protocols addressing medication management, falls, dementia, and caregiver burden?
o: An adult day health program providing structured daytime care.
A home nursing program providing medication administration support.
The GRACE program integrating primary care and a geriatrics team.
A dementia medication program focused on donepezil dose adjustment.
explanation:
**GRACE** integrates geriatric and primary care, with an advanced practice nurse and social worker collaborating with primary care and an interdisciplinary team (p. 200). Protocols include "medication management, difficulty walking/falls" and "dementia, and caregiver burden" (p. 201). This identifies the model with those protocols; the scenario does not establish program eligibility.

**A. An adult day health program providing structured daytime care.** Wrong, the named protocols belong to the GRACE model, not to the daytime service described here (pp. 200-201).
**B. A home nursing program providing medication administration support.** Wrong, medication administration addresses one need; the source assigns the combined protocols to GRACE (pp. 200-201).
**C. The GRACE program integrating primary care and a geriatrics team.** Correct, the source explicitly lists these needs among GRACE protocols and describes its integration with primary care (pp. 200-201).
**D. A dementia medication program focused on donepezil dose adjustment.** Wrong, dose adjustment is not the interdisciplinary model to which the source assigns these protocols (pp. 200-201).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 200, 201.
ref: Hazzard Ch 14 — MODELS OF HOSPITAL AND OUTPATIENT CARE
chapterTitle: Models of Hospital and Outpatient Care

q: A 72-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and recently diagnosed mild cognitive impairment (MoCA 22/30) receives home-based primary care. Her daughter found her unconscious twice in the past month, both times early in the morning before breakfast. She takes glimepiride 4 mg twice daily, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, and lisinopril 10 mg daily. Her latest HbA1c is 6.8%, creatinine clearance is 58 mL/min, and prebreakfast fingerstick glucose readings range from 68 to 95 mg/dL. Which approach to the sulfonylurea agrees with Hazzard when hypoglycemia is a concern?
o: Stop glimepiride and follow glucose to reassess treatment needs.
Continue glimepiride at a reduced dose to retain sulfonylurea treatment.
Replace glimepiride with glipizide to retain treatment from the same class.
Replace glimepiride with glyburide to retain treatment from the same class.
explanation:
**Sulfonylureas** increase insulin secretion, and hypoglycemia is their main adverse effect. Hazzard advises avoiding this class when there is concern about hypoglycemia, even though individual agents differ in risk; the low readings and episodes in this vignette make that concern relevant without proving the cause of the unconsciousness (p. 1579).
"Their primary mechanism of action is to enhance insulin secretion by the β-cells of the endocrine pancreas." (p. 1579).

**A. Stop glimepiride and follow glucose to reassess treatment needs.** Correct, discontinuation follows the source advice to avoid sulfonylureas when hypoglycemia is a concern; glucose follow-up allows reassessment after removing the drug (p. 1579; clinical application).
**B. Continue glimepiride at a reduced dose to retain sulfonylurea treatment.** Wrong, a reduced dose still retains a sulfonylurea, whereas the source advises avoiding the class when hypoglycemia is a concern (p. 1579).
**C. Replace glimepiride with glipizide to retain treatment from the same class.** Wrong, glipizide may be safer than other agents, but the same paragraph advises avoiding the whole class when hypoglycemia is a concern (p. 1579).
**D. Replace glimepiride with glyburide to retain treatment from the same class.** Wrong, glyburide is not recommended in older patients because its long half-life is associated with greater hypoglycemia risk (p. 1579).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1579.

q: חולה עם ICD מבקש שינוי בטיפול בסוף החיים. לפני החלת חוק החולה הנוטה למות, מי מוסמך לקבוע שהמטופל הוא חולה הנוטה למות לפי החוק?
o: בן המשפחה הקרוב על סמך היכרותו עם רצונות המטופל
טכנאי המכשיר על סמך מספר השוקים שניתנו באשפוז
הרופא האחראי על סמך מצבו הרפואי ולאחר התייעצות
ועדת האתיקה על סמך עצם בקשתו לשנות את הטיפול
explanation:
תחולת הוראות **חוק החולה הנוטה למות** תלויה בקביעה רפואית לפי החוק. הרופא האחראי מוסמך לקבוע את המצב הרפואי ונדרש להתייעץ ברופאים המומחים המטפלים; בקשה לשינוי טיפול במכשיר אינה כשלעצמה קביעה זו (עמ׳ 6 ו־7).
"רופא אחראי מוסמך לקבוע כי המטופל הוא חולה הנוטה למות, אם נוכח כי המטופל סובל מבעיה רפואית חשוכת מרפא" (עמ׳ 6).
"קביעת רופא אחראי לפי סעיף זה תיעשה לאחר התייעצות עם הרופאים המומחים המטפלים במטופל ובמידת האפשר גם עם רופאו האישי." (עמ׳ 7).

**א. בן המשפחה הקרוב על סמך היכרותו עם רצונות המטופל.** שגויה, היכרות עם רצונות המטופל אינה מחליפה את הקביעה הרפואית שהחוק מפקיד בידי הרופא האחראי (עמ׳ 6 ו־7).
**ב. טכנאי המכשיר על סמך מספר השוקים שניתנו באשפוז.** שגויה, נתוני המכשיר אינם מקנים לטכנאי סמכות לקבוע את המעמד הרפואי על פי החוק (עמ׳ 6 ו־7).
**ג. הרופא האחראי על סמך מצבו הרפואי ולאחר התייעצות.** נכונה, הסמכות וההתייעצות מוגדרות בסעיף 8, והן קודמות ליישום ההוראות התלויות במעמד זה (עמ׳ 6 ו־7).
**ד. ועדת האתיקה על סמך עצם בקשתו לשנות את הטיפול.** שגויה, הבקשה לשינוי טיפול אינה מחליפה את הקביעה של הרופא האחראי לפי סעיף 8 (עמ׳ 6 ו־7).

מקור: חוק החולה הנוטה למות, סעיף 8, עמ׳ 6, 7.

q: בן 57 מתחיל לפתח הפרעות בזיכרון ובעיות בתפקודים ניהוליים. אמו סבלה ממחלת אלצהיימר ונפטרה בגיל 68, דוד שלו אובחן כלוקה במחלת אלצהיימר בגיל 61 ונפטר בגיל 73. מה נכון בנוגע לסיכון שלו לפתח מחלת אלצהיימר?
o: אם ימצא גן הגורם למחלתו, ככל הנראה מדובר בפגם בגן הפריסינלין (PSEN1)
ברוב המקרים של Early Onset Alzheimer, ניתן למצוא סיבה גנטית ברורה
אם המטופל הטרוזיגוטי לגן APOE ε4 הסיכוי להתפתחות מחלת אלצהיימר מעל 50%
הגן ל- MAPT (Microtubule Associated Protein Tau) מנבא התדרדרות מהירה יותר במחלת אלצהיימר
explanation:
Early onset with a family history raises suspicion of **familial Alzheimer disease**. The genes described are APP, PSEN1, and PSEN2; PSEN1 accounts for most identified familial mutations. Young age at onset must be distinguished from familial disease with a proven mutation (pp. 897–898).

**A. If a causative gene is found, PSEN1 is the most likely defect.** Correct, most of the described familial mutations occur in this gene, fitting the conditional wording of the option (p. 897).
**B. A clear genetic cause can be found in most early-onset Alzheimer cases.** Wrong, the book distinguishes these groups and reports that known genes explain only some familial cases; young age alone does not establish an identifiable mutation (p. 897).
**C. APOE ε4 heterozygosity implies a probability of Alzheimer disease above 50%.** Wrong, the source describes increased relative risk, not this absolute probability; APOE ε4 alone is insufficient to cause the disease (p. 898).
**D. MAPT predicts more rapid deterioration in Alzheimer disease.** Wrong, MAPT mutations are described in frontotemporal lobar degeneration, not as a marker of Alzheimer progression in this question (pp. 873, 897–898).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 873, 897–898.

q: מה נכון לגבי השפעה של אצטילכולין על תהליכים ותפקודים בגוף?
o: הוא מופרש אך ורק במוח
הוא לא משפיע על יכולת למידה וזיכרון
הפרשת יתר של אצטילכולין יכולה לגרום לבלבול, הפרעות בהתנהגות והזיות ראייה
הפחתת מספר נוירונים במעיים שמפרישים אצטילכולין היא אחת מהסיבות של עצירות
explanation:
Official answer: ד

**Acetylcholine acts in the enteric nervous system as well as the brain**. Loss of enteric neurons may contribute to reduced propulsive colonic activity and constipation, but this is not an inevitable consequence of healthy aging (p. 1356).

**A. It is secreted only in the brain.** Wrong, the source explicitly describes acetylcholine-producing enteric neurons, so its activity is not restricted to the brain (p. 1356).
**B. It does not affect learning or memory.** Wrong, acetylcholinesterase inhibitors increase cholinergic activity in cognitive brain systems; this does not fit a claim of no role in learning or memory (pp. 910–911).
**C. Excess acetylcholine secretion can cause confusion, behavioral disturbance and visual hallucinations.** Wrong, not officially accepted. The source identifies anticholinergic medications as inducing or worsening delirium; it does not support attributing this symptom complex here to excess acetylcholine secretion (p. 883).
**D. Fewer acetylcholine-producing intestinal neurons contribute to constipation.** Correct, reduced numbers of enteric neurons producing acetylcholine and nitric oxide are proposed as a mechanism of reduced propulsion and longer transit in older people with constipation (p. 1356).

Source-to-key qualification: This is a possible mechanism. The source does not say that every healthy older person develops this abnormality (p. 1356).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1356, 910, 911, 883.

q: בת 78, לאחר שבץ מוחי איסכמי מסוג Watershed משמאל. מסוגלת לחזור במדויק על משפטים קצרים וארוכים, אך מתקשה ליזום דיבור ספונטני. הבנה שמורה. באיזה סוג אפזיה סביר שמדובר?
o: Expressive Aphasia (Broca)
Receptive Aphasia (Wernicke)
Transcortical Motor Aphasia
Conduction Aphasia
explanation:
**Preserved repetition** with nonfluent spontaneous speech and preserved comprehension is the combination described for **transcortical motor aphasia** (Hazzard 8e, p. 138, Table 9-4).

**A. Expressive aphasia (Broca).** Wrong, speech is nonfluent but repetition is impaired; preserved repetition here does not fit (p. 138).
**B. Receptive aphasia (Wernicke).** Wrong, spoken comprehension and repetition are impaired, whereas both are preserved here (p. 138).
**C. Transcortical motor aphasia.** Correct, the table combines nonfluency, good comprehension and normal repetition, matching the described language disturbance (p. 138).
**D. Conduction aphasia.** Wrong, repetition is impaired and speech is fluent, unlike the normal repetition and nonfluency in the stem (p. 138).

Source: Hazzard 8e, p. 138, Table 9-4.

q: מה מהווה גורם לפרוגנוזה ירודה ב- Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) בזקנים?
o: שכיחות נמוכה של קריוטיפ 5q- 7q-
ביטוי מופחת של מסלולי TNF ו- RAS במח העצם
שכיחות גבוהה של MDS ברקע
רגישות מוגברת לאפופטוזיס של התאים הבלסטים
explanation:
In older adults with **AML**, preceding myelodysplastic syndromes and poor-prognosis karyotypes are more frequent, alongside biological treatment resistance. The source describes increased signaling-pathway expression and reduced blast-cell propensity for apoptosis after induction therapy (pp. 1385–1386).

**A. Low frequency of 5q- and 7q- karyotypes.** Wrong, these poor-prognosis karyotypes occur at high, not low, frequency and contribute to the treatment difficulty described (p. 1385).
**B. Reduced TNF and RAS pathway expression in marrow.** Wrong, the source describes increased ras and tumor necrosis factor pathway expression. Reduced expression does not match the biology offered to explain worse survival (p. 1386).
**C. High frequency of preceding MDS.** Correct, preceding myelodysplastic syndromes are explicitly among the findings associated with poorer prognosis and treatment outcomes (p. 1385).
**D. Greater blast-cell susceptibility to apoptosis.** Wrong, after traditional induction, blasts from older patients show lower propensity for apoptosis. Increased susceptibility to cell death is not the explanation for the poorer outcome described (p. 1386).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1385, 1386.
